source: Arbitration D0142, read from C048_rev.webp (the only photo of C048): the reverse shows the large 1 / DEUTSCHE MARK / 1993 with oak sprigs; there is NO letter above the digit 1 - the only stroke there is the top of the '1' itself. The Gemini claim ('J' above the 1) reads the denomination digit's own top stroke. The 1 Mark's mint letter sits on the eagle obverse, which was never photographed for C048, so the photo cannot support 'J'. Record ['D'] stands.

Arbitration D0143, read from C196_obv.webp: after the date 1987 there is a separator dot and then the rim legend (DEUTSCHLAND) in legend-sized letters; there is no small mint letter to the right of the date. On this pfennig type the mintmark is on the reverse, above the denomination between the rye ears - the reverse was never photographed for C196. The Gemini claim ('G' right of the date) reads legend text. Record ['F'] stands.

Arbitration D0144, read from C177_obv.webp: the date at the bottom of the obverse reads 2009 - digit by digit 2-0-0-9; the final digit is a closed loop with a descending tail (a 9), not the flat-topped 5 the Gemini claim reports. The specimen's recorded mintage (132,960,300) is also the 2009 Royal Shield 1-pound mintage. Record 2009 stands.

Arbitration D0145, read from C228_obv.webp: the bottom of the obverse reads '1989' followed by a separator dot and the rim legend; there is no letter 'J' after the year. On this pfennig type the mintmark is on the reverse above the denomination, which was never photographed for C228. The Gemini claim reads the separator/legend as a mint letter. Record ['G'] stands.

Arbitration D0146, read from C237_obv.webp: the date reads 1971, followed by a separator dot and the rim legend (DEUTSCHLAND); there is no mint letter after the date on this side. On this pfennig type the mintmark is on the reverse above the denomination, never photographed for C237. The Gemini claim ('G' after 1971) reads legend text. Record ['D'] stands.

Arbitration D0147, read from C018_obv.webp: the 'D' at the bottom right is the final letter of the rim legend DEUTSCHLAND, at full legend size and spacing - it is legend text, not a mintmark. On this pfennig type the mintmark is on the reverse above the denomination, never photographed for C018. The Gemini claim mistakes the legend's last letter for a mint letter. Record ['G'] stands.

Arbitration D0148, read from C225_obv.webp (worn, low contrast; read on contrast-stretched and inverted zooms of the bottom band): the date's last two glyphs both carry a 7's structure - a top bar with a diagonal descending to the lower left. A final '1' (the Gemini claim, 1971) would be a bare vertical stroke with no top bar; the fourth glyph has the top bar. Read: 1977, with the wear caveat noted. Record 1977 stands.
